title: Use a multi-variable graph or table to support or weaken a researcher's claim
subtitle: Command of Evidence · 76 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **76 of the official questions in Command of Evidence are this one** — 9 Easy, 22 Medium, 45 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- This is a hard data question.

- There is a graph or table with several series, conditions or groups, a longer passage describing a study, and a stem asking which choice uses the data to support, weaken or illustrate the researchers' conclusion or hypothesis.
- Sometimes the stem is a 'which finding' question tied to a chart, and sometimes the passage defines a ratio or combination you must compute.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Write down the conclusion's precise condition: which group, which variable, and which direction.
- Note whether it applies only under certain conditions.
- 2) Map that onto the chart's legend and axes, finding exactly which series or cells must be compared.
- 3) Check each choice for accuracy, then keep the one that makes the comparison the claim requires.
- Compute any ratio the passage defines instead of reading raw values.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick a choice that accurately describes the chart but compares the wrong series, ignores the condition the claim depends on (such as among participants with high scores, or under the maximum-temperature scenario), or uses raw values when the claim depends on a ratio the passage defined.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
